archetype.name: Pocket Passer (accuracy-first)
archetype.definition: A 36-year-old rhythm thrower who wins with ball placement on short and intermediate timing routes. He is not a creator outside the structure: his legs add nothing and he takes too many sacks.

report.headline: The Seattle-era accuracy is back, propped up by 18 deep balls
report.take:
Geno Smith's 2025 in Las Vegas looked like the end: -0.1 EPA per play (49th of 63), a league-worst 17 interceptions and a 2-13 record. Seven games into his return to New York, the passer from his 2022-24 Seattle run has reappeared. He completes 70% (6th), his CPOE is back to 3.96 after 0.7 last year, and his yards per attempt have jumped from 6.75 to 7.84. The style hasn't changed: intended air yards around 7, throws landing short of the sticks, and a time to throw (2.92) and aggressiveness (15.46%) almost identical to last season. What changed is that the throws are landing.

The efficiency is highly concentrated. Garrett Wilson has 52 targets at 0.459 EPA each, a 23.9-point total that nearly matches the 24.9 Smith has added on all his dropbacks. The 18 throws of 20-plus air yards have produced 33.5 EPA, with 4 touchdowns and a 28.9 CPOE. That is more than his entire dropback total, which means the other 222 dropbacks, sacks included, netted out below zero. His short game is genuinely good (0.201 EPA on 117 throws 0-9 yards). The screens behind the line (-9.1) and the designed runs (-7.0) give a chunk of it back.

The ugly parts are structural. His 9.2% sack rate ranks 38th of 45, and 39.6% of his pressures become sacks. That isn't new: his pressure-to-sack rate was 0.355 in 2024 and 0.462 last year, and his line ranks 27th in hits allowed. Ten of his 21 sacks came on third down, where the Jets convert 35.4%. The game-state split is the most telling. Trailing by 9 or more, he's at 0.489 EPA per play. Within one score he's at -0.002, and in close fourth quarters he's at -0.247. A lot of the shine comes when defenses are protecting a lead.

Expect a competent, accurate starter whose weekly output swings with whether the shot plays hit. His game EPA has ranged from -11.3 against Cleveland to 12.2 against Miami. A 1% interception rate from a quarterback who threw 15 and 17 the last two years is the number most likely to move against him, and it's already ticking up over the last three weeks.

strengths.title: Accuracy back to Seattle form
strengths.body: His 3.96 CPOE and 70% completion rate (6th) put him back alongside his 2022 and 2024 seasons, when he posted CPOEs above 5. His bad-throw rate has been low for years, so this looks like a return to baseline, and 2025 looks like the outlier. That gives his floor real durability as long as the protection lets him set his feet.

strengths.title: Wilson and the 10-plus-yard window
strengths.body: Throws of 10 or more air yards return 1.001 EPA each with a 15.5 CPOE, and Wilson is the engine at 0.459 EPA per target. The intermediate level (0.516 EPA on 32 throws) is a sturdier base than the deep ball. The 18-attempt deep sample will cool, but a reliable connection with his top receiver should hold up.

strengths.title: Efficient short-area rhythm game
strengths.body: On 117 throws of 0-9 air yards he's at 0.201 EPA with a 54.7% success rate and a 3.6 CPOE. That is the bread and butter of a low-aDOT offense, and it doesn't depend on explosive plays. It's the most repeatable part of his profile.

concerns.title: Sacks are a trait, not a blip
concerns.body: A 9.2% sack rate (38th) comes from two things. First, he converts pressure into sacks at a high clip (39.6%, 34th of 38), as he did in 2024 and 2025. Second, his line allows the sixth-most hits. He doesn't scramble enough to pay for holding the ball: 10 scrambles, 4.2% of dropbacks. With a starting guard out, this is not likely to improve soon.

concerns.title: Thin when the game is close
concerns.body: Within one score he's at -0.002 EPA per play. In close fourth quarters he's at -0.247, while trailing by 9+ he's at 0.489. Third downs bring 10 sacks and a 35.4% conversion rate. Some of this is the protection and the 2-5 record creating catch-up scripts, but the leverage downs are where his sack habit costs the most.

concerns.title: Interception luck likely to fade
concerns.body: A 1% interception rate is out of character for a passer who led the league in picks last year, and his last three games already show a 2.2% rate. The 28.9 CPOE on deep throws won't survive more attempts either. When both normalize, the gap between him and the league's average passer narrows.

trend.note: His game EPA has whipsawed: 10.9 at Detroit, then -4.9 and -11.3 against Chicago and Cleveland, then back to 12.2 against Miami. Over the last three games his EPA per dropback (0.068) sits below his season mark, with more interceptions.

nextGame.headline: Raiders' soft underneath defense fits his short game; pressure is the risk
nextGame.body:
Las Vegas is a good draw for the way Smith actually plays. The Raiders rank 23rd in pass EPA and 27th in success rate, and they are dead last against short throws (0.295 EPA). They also allow quarterbacks 20.1 PPR points (28th) and 2.57 touchdowns a game (29th). The catch is the part of his game that has inflated his season. Their deep EPA allowed ranks 9th, so the shot plays may not be there, and the game likely runs through the 0-9 yard area. Their 4th-ranked hit rate is also a direct threat to a line that ranks 27th in hits allowed. The Raiders' offense passes efficiently (9th) and can't run (31st), which leans toward a game with real passing volume. The 45.5 total is higher than most of his games.

Availability tilts against his protection and supporting cast. Guard Dylan Parham (86% of snaps) is out, weakening the interior against a defense that gets home. Breece Hall is out too. That puts more on Braelon Allen, whose 20 targets have returned -0.209 EPA each, so checkdowns to the backfield are a drag rather than an outlet. The Raiders' injury report is mostly on their offense, and no defensive starter of note is listed.

keyMatchups.title: Short throws vs league's worst coverage
keyMatchups.body: His 0.201 EPA on short throws meets the defense that allows the most EPA there. This is the cleanest edge of the week and the most repeatable one. If Smith stays patient underneath, the efficiency should come without needing the deep ball.

keyMatchups.title: Raiders' pass rush vs a weakened line
keyMatchups.body: Las Vegas hits quarterbacks at the 4th-highest rate. Smith's line already ranks 27th and now loses a starting guard. Given his pressure-to-sack habit, every extra hit raises the odds of a drive-killing sack.

keyMatchups.title: Wilson against a sticky WR1 defense
keyMatchups.body: Opposing WR1s score 2.9 PPR under their averages against Las Vegas (8th), even though their EPA per target is middling (22nd). Paired with a top-10 deep defense, that suggests the Raiders limit volume and big plays to top receivers. Tight ends draw 29.5% of targets against them versus a 24% league share, which points to Mason Taylor as the release valve.

nextGame.watch: How many times he's sacked on third down. If he gets the ball out underneath against a soft short defense, this is a 250-yard, two-score day. If he holds it against their rush, the drives die.

restOfSeason.body:
The accuracy and the short-to-intermediate efficiency are real. They match what he did for three years in Seattle, and last season looks like the aberration. The two numbers that will move against him are the deep-ball returns (18 attempts at 1.863 EPA cannot hold) and the 1% interception rate. Expect his efficiency to settle closer to his 2023-24 level, around 0.07-0.08 EPA per play, than the 0.118 per dropback he carries now. That still makes him an above-average starter on a team that passes less than expected.

Volume should stay modest at around 28-31 attempts. Sacks will keep pace near three a game unless the line gets healthier. Touchdown output depends on game script, since a 2-5 team chasing points has fed his best numbers. I'd project roughly 215-260 passing yards, 1.2-1.8 touchdowns, and an interception rate that pushes back toward one every other game or so.
swingFactors: Pass protection with Parham out and a 27th-ranked hit rate
Whether the deep connection with Wilson keeps hitting

confidence.note: Seven starts and a career baseline support the accuracy rebound, but the deep-ball sample is only 18 throws.
